row: | DOC-A.1-6 | **Alignment of alphanumeric group items (and strongly-typed group items) relative to the first item within the group**, §8.5.1.6.1 · §8.5.1.6.5, required + documented | **Always coincident.** Every alphanumeric group item, and every strongly-typed group item (a group declared by a `TYPEDEF STRONG` type, 2002 onward), starts at the same byte as the first item subordinate to it, whatever that item's class or usage: COBOL.NET never places slack bytes ahead of a group's first item, and none between items either (no automatic alignment, item 7; no alignment or implicit FILLER for SYNCHRONIZED, item 195). A group's size is therefore exactly the sum of its subordinate items' sizes: `05 G1 PIC 9(4) COMP` followed by `05 G2 PIC X` is a 3-byte group whose first two bytes are G1, and a strongly-typed group of `9(4) COMP-5` then `X` is likewise 3 bytes. The standard's own exceptions (the group coincident with a first item that is national, boolean, message-tag, object or pointer; the type's essential characteristics preserved) hold because there is no other case. The same answer at every edition; one layout authority computes every offset and size (`RecordLayout.OffsetOf`, `RecordLayout.PhysicalWidth`). | — |

record.notes: Row written from the code: RecordLayout.PhysicalWidth sums subordinate widths with no padding term and OffsetOf advances by the same widths, so every group (alphanumeric or strongly-typed) is coincident with its first item. row: | DOC-A.1-8 | **ALPHABET clause — ordinal number of characters in the native coded character sets**, §12.3.7.4 GR6, required + documented | **Code-unit order: the ordinal position of a native character is its UTF-16 code unit plus one**, in BOTH native sets. The native alphanumeric and the native national coded character sets are each the 65,536 UTF-16 code units, one per character position (item 33), ordered by code-unit value: X"00" (U+0000) is ordinal 1, `"A"` is 66, X"FF" is 256, `"€"` (U+20AC) is 8,365, and U+FFFF is 65,536; the national set uses the same numbering (`N"A"` is 66). These are the ordinals FUNCTION ORD returns and FUNCTION CHAR / CHAR-NATIONAL accept whenever no ALPHABET names a different program collating sequence (`CobolIntrinsics.Ord`, `CobolIntrinsics.Char`, `CobolIntrinsics.CharNational`); an ordinal outside 1–65,536 sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. The same numbering at every edition (the national set exists from 2002). ⚠ HIGH-VALUE and the figurative extremes are still computed over U+0000–U+00FF rather than the whole native set (kb/Work PB1093, open). | — |

record.notes: Row written from CobolIntrinsics.Text.cs: Ord(string) = s[0]+1; Char(long)/CharNational(long) accept 1..65536 (c = n-1, > 0xFFFF refused with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION). row: | DOC-A.1-9 | **Alphanumeric literals — number of hexadecimal digits that map to an alphanumeric character**, §8.3.3.2.3 SR6, required + documented | **Two.** Each pair of hexadecimal digits in a hexadecimal alphanumeric literal (`X"…"`, §8.3.3.2.2 format 2) is ONE alphanumeric character whose code is the pair's value: `X"41424344"` is `"ABCD"`, `X"4a4B"` is `"JK"` (either case of A–F), and `FUNCTION LENGTH(X"414243")` is 3. A literal whose digit count is not a whole number of pairs violates §8.3.3.2.3 SR6 and is rejected with **COBOLNET1635** (`X"414"`, `X"4"`), in a VALUE clause and in a procedure statement alike (`CobolLiteral.HexGroupViolation`, decoded by `CobolLiteral.DecodeHex`). The national twin, four digits per national character, is item 122. ⚠ kb/Work PB1393 (open): the COBOLNET1635 check is not yet applied to a hexadecimal literal written as an operand of a concatenation expression (`"Z" & X"4"`) or inside a keyword-omitted intrinsic argument. | `conformance:negative/r03-hex-literal-digit-grouping` |

row: | DOC-A.1-12 | **Byte — number of bits in**, §8.1.2, required + documented | **Eight**, on every supported computer (COBOL.NET's one target is the .NET runtime, whose byte is 8 bits). Every byte count the compiler reports or lays out rests on it: a `USAGE BIT` item of `PIC 1(8)` occupies exactly one byte and one of `PIC 1(9)` or `PIC 1(12)` occupies two (a partial trailing byte counts whole), `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH` counts 8-bit bytes (`PIC X(4)` is 4, `PIC 9(4) COMP` is 2, `PIC N(2)` is 4), and a record written to a file is a sequence of 8-bit bytes. The bit-to-byte law is `BitLayout.BitsPerCharacter` (= 8) through `BitLayout.Characters`. The same answer at every edition. | `conformance:2002/l1_byte_length_implicit_filler` |

row: | DOC-A.1-16 | **CALL statement — calling a non-COBOL program**, §14.9.4.4 GR3g, required + documented | **Not possible: COBOL.NET executes no non-COBOL program through CALL.** A CALL resolves only to a COBOL.NET program — one in the run unit, or a separately compiled COBOL.NET module `<program-name>.dll` in the application directory that carries the COBOL.NET module registrar (`ProgramTable.ProbeSiblingModule`). Every other target, including a .NET assembly that is present in the application directory (`CALL "Antlr4.Runtime.Standard"`) or a system library name held in an identifier, is **not located**, so GR3g's non-COBOL branch is never reached: the CALL is unsuccessful with **EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND** (GR3b) and continues per GR3h — the ON EXCEPTION imperative statement when one is written (ON OVERFLOW before 2023), otherwise the exception processing of item 17. There is no CALL-CONVENTION directive (§7.3.9), so a program cannot be declared non-COBOL either (item 19); program-name formation and locating for non-COBOL programs (items 13 and 15) therefore never arise. The same at every edition. | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-17 | **CALL statement — other effects of an unsuccessful CALL whose exception condition is handled by exception processing**, §14.9.4.4 GR3h item 2, required + documented | **None beyond the transfer of control.** GR3h item 2 applies when the called program was not successfully called (EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, -PTR-NULL, -RESOURCES, -ARG-MISMATCH, -RECURSIVE-CALL or an EC-EXTERNAL condition), checking for that condition is enabled, and no ON EXCEPTION phrase is written (a NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase alone does not count). The applicable declarative runs; if it returns control with `RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT`, execution continues after the end of the CALL statement, and the CALL has had no other effect: **no program is activated or placed in its initial state, every USING argument and the RETURNING item keep the values they held before the CALL** (`CALL "NOSUCHPG" USING X RETURNING R` leaves `X` = `"ABCD"` and `R` = 1234), NOT ON EXCEPTION is not executed, and `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS` names the condition until the next one. A declarative that ends without RESUME has no next executable statement for a fatal condition (§14.6.3), so the run unit terminates abnormally (§14.6.12). The routing is `CallEmitter`'s exception partition (kb/Work PB233). 2002 onward (the exception-condition model). | — |

record.notes: Probes /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i17.cob (>>TURN EC-PROGRAM CHECKING ON, USE AFTER EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND with RESUME NEXT STATEMENT; --std 2002 and 2023): 'DECL EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND', NOT ON EXCEPTION not executed, 'AFTER R=1234 X=ABCD'; i17b.cob (no RESUME) -> declarative then abnormal run-unit termination (consistent with §14.6.3's rule that a fatal-condition declarative has no next executable statement — cite.py --check 14.6.3 OK); i17c.cob (no >>TURN, no ON EXCEPTION) -> abnormal termination (GR3h item 3, not this item). The GR3h routing half is pinned by conformance:2023/pb233_call_exception_partition arm A, but that golden does not discriminate THIS determination (arguments/RETURNING untouched), so Pinned-by is —. PARTIAL: only the EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND arm was probed for the argument/RETURNING effect; the -ARG-MISMATCH / -RECURSIVE-CALL / EC-EXTERNAL arms are claimed from CallEmitter's single partition by reading (i17r2.cob reached EC-PROGRAM-RECURSIVE-CALL in a callee without a declarative, so the RESUME path for it was not exercised). cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 'All other effects of the CALL statement are defined by the implementor' OK (3h2). Owning note: A11.

row: | DOC-A.1-21 | **CHAR function — which one of the multiple characters is returned**, §15.15.4 r2 (second sentence), required + documented | The alphanumeric twin of item 22. §15.15.4 r2 has two branches and only the second is an implementor obligation. **Branch 1 — the order is DEFINED** (an `ALPHABET` literal phrase with `ALSO`): the standard answers, and COBOL.NET returns the first character defined for the position — under `ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B" "D"` as the program collating sequence, `FUNCTION CHAR(FUNCTION ORD("A"))` is `"C"` (`LiteralPhraseCollation.CharAt`). **Branch 2 — the order is UNDEFINED, and this is item 21:** an `ALPHABET … IS LOCALE` sequence is an algorithm, not a written order, so every set of characters the locale collates equally shares one ordinal position with no order among its members. **COBOL.NET returns the LOWEST-CODED member of that rank** (`LocaleCollation.CharAt` reading `OrderVector.FirstOfRank`, materialized once per collator), so the answer is the same for every invocation at a given implementation, collating sequence and ordinal position: X"00", X"01" and X"1F" all share ordinal 1 of a locale sequence, and `FUNCTION CHAR(1)` is X"00". 2002 onward (the LOCALE phrase). | — |

record.notes: Verified by reading LocaleCollation.CharAt (returns OrderVector.FirstOfRank[position], the lowest code unit collating at that rank; field comment cites §15.15.4 r2) and by probes: /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i21.cob (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS LOC, ALPHABET LOC IS LOCALE; --std 2002 and 2023): ORD(X"00")=ORD(X"01")=ORD(X"1F")=1, CHAR(1) -> CONVERT(..ANY ANUM HEX)=00, stable across two invocations; i21b.cob (ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B" "D"; --std 85 and 2023): ORD("A")=1, CHAR(1)=C (branch 1, standard-defined; pinned separately by conformance:2002/pb59_char_representative, which does not pin this determination). No alphanumeric twin of l1_char_national_locale_tie exists, so Pinned-by is —. cite.py --check 15.15.4 'If the order of multiple characters having the same position is undefined, the implementor shall define which of those multiple characters is returned' OK (2); 12.3.7.4 'Literal-1 is the first character in the sequence ...' OK. Owning note: A11.

evidence: LocaleCollation.cs:129-132 CharAt, :147 FirstOfRank; probes i21.cob (ORD00=ORD01=ORD1F=1, HEX=00), i21b.cob (ORDA=1 CHAR=C); cite 15.15.4 2) OK

row: | DOC-A.1-26 | **COBOL character repertoire — more than one encoding in a compilation group, and the control functions that switch between them**, §8.1.3.2 GR2, conditionally required (provided) + documented | **Provided, per FILE, by byte-order mark; there are no control functions.** Every file of a compilation group — the source file named on the command line and each library text a COPY statement brings in — is decoded independently, so one compilation group may mix encodings file by file. A file that begins with a byte-order mark is read in the encoding the mark names: UTF-8 (EF BB BF), UTF-16 little- or big-endian (FF FE / FE FF), or UTF-32; a file with no byte-order mark is read as UTF-8. The mark itself is not source text. The encoding cannot change inside a file: no in-stream control function or directive switches it, and none is part of the syntax. A UTF-8 main program that COPYs a UTF-16LE library text holding `VALUE "O€K"` compiles and displays `O€K`. Both source text and library text are read by `CompilationInputs.ReadAllText`. The same at every edition. | — |

row: | DOC-A.1-29 | **Compile-time arithmetic — mode of arithmetic used and rules for intermediate data handling**, §7.3.6 (§7.3.6.3 GR2 · §7.3.6.2 SR2), required + documented | **A mode unique to compile-time arithmetic: .NET `System.Decimal`**, the same for a constant entry (`CONSTANT AS`), a `>>DEFINE` value and a `>>IF`/`>>EVALUATE` operand (one evaluator, `CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator`). It is neither a §8.8.1 standard mode nor the runtime's native arithmetic. **Precision and range:** each intermediate result is a decimal number of up to 28–29 significant digits (at most 28 of them after the decimal point) whose magnitude is below about 7.9×10²⁸; an intermediate result outside that range is a compile-time error — COBOLNET1547 in a constant entry, COBOLNET1619 in a directive — never a wrapped or truncated value (`9999999999999999999999999999 * 10` is refused). **Intermediate rounding:** addition, subtraction, multiplication and division are exact whenever the exact result fits those digits; otherwise the result is **rounded to the nearest representable value, a tie to the even digit** — division does NOT truncate: `2 / 3 * 3` is 2 and `100 / 7 * 7` is 100 (a truncating division would give 1 and 99), while `1 / 3 * 3` is 0; `0.0000000000000000000000000005 / 2 * 10000000000000000000000000000` is 2 and `0.0000000000000000000000000015 / 2 * 10000000000000000000000000000` is 8. **Final result:** truncated toward zero to its integer part, as §7.3.6.3 GR3 requires (`-7 / 2` is -3, `2.5 + 0` is 2). The exponentiation operator (§7.3.6.2 SR1a) and a division by zero (SR1c) are rejected. 2002 onward. | — |

record.notes: Row written from CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator: EvalArith rides System.Decimal (+,-,*,/ with OverflowException -> CtDiagCode.ArithmeticRule; '/' by zero rejected), EvaluateArithmeticOperand applies decimal.Truncate to an expression's final result. Probes /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i29.cob (--std 2002 and 2023): C1 2/3*3=2, C2 100/7*7=100, C3 1/3*3=0, C4 (2.5e-28 tie) =2, C5 (7.5e-28 tie) =8 -> round-half-even, C6 -7/2=-3, C7 exact product 11111111111110888888888888, C8 2.5+0=2; i29b.cob overflow -> COBOLNET1547; i29c.cob >>DEFINE X AS 7 / 2 * 2 -> 7 (same evaluator). ⚠ docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 bullet 'Compile-time arithmetic mode' (line 504) contradicts this row ('standard fixed-point decimal mode', 'division truncates', multiplication exact) — kb/Work PB1369 (open) owns that bullet; the integrator should replace it with a pointer to this row in the same change set. cite.py --check 7.3.6.3 'The implementor shall define and document which mode of arithmetic ...' OK (2); 7.3.6.2 'They shall also document which intermediate rounding method is used' OK (2); 7.3.6.3 'The final result ... truncated to the integer part' OK (3). No spec-derived pin (constant_entry / directive_expressions do not discriminate rounding) — row says —.

row: | DOC-A.1-32 | **Computer's coded character set — coded character values for certain COBOL items**, §8.1.2, required + documented | **Fixed at compile time; the same UTF-16 code unit in the alphanumeric and the national set** (the two native sets share one code-unit numbering, item 33), so each element's alphanumeric and national values are identical and therefore equivalent. Figurative constants: **SPACE** U+0020, **QUOTE** U+0022 (the quotation mark), **ZERO** U+0030. **Space filling** of alphanumeric and national items: U+0020 (`MOVE "A" TO` a `PIC X(4)` item stores 41 20 20 20). Editing characters: **B** inserts U+0020 (the same value as SPACE and space fill), **0** U+0030 (the same value as ZERO and the digit 0), digits **0–9** U+0030–U+0039, **C R** U+0043 U+0052, **D B** U+0044 U+0042, **E** U+0045, **-** U+002D, **+** U+002B, **\*** U+002A, **/** U+002F, **,** U+002C, **.** U+002E. The **default currency string** for the `$` symbol is `$` U+0024. None of these values depends on the run-time environment. The figurative values come from `FigurativeConstants.FillChar`. The same at every edition (national data from 2002). | — |
